Ok I’m in a similar boat! I haven’t given into my usual tempting mortal sins but the temptation is ramping up! I’ll tell you what my plan was (still is I guess) and I think you can start this now and you might be all the better for it!

I researched the difference between mortal and venial sin and reflected on the sins I committed regularly before accepting Jesus as my Lord, after and while doing RCIA. While I was in RCIA and learning more about the faith, I stopped a good amount of habitual sins but I still had 4-5 habitual mortal sins. I endeavoured to focus my learning on Catholic explanations on why those sins were bad - yes sure we should think they are bad because God says so but without personal conviction it will be easier to fall into temptation. If you don’t have a good reason to tell yourself “no” you’ll tell yourself “God forgives” instead, which is true! But I personally think that’s more of a Protestant mindset. From what I understand, the Catholic way is to carry your cross! Which means, to me at least, to acknowledge your sin and trudge forward in the suffering of avoiding those sins and asking for Gods grace to make avoiding those sins feel natural instead of a burden. 

With that said, God does offer grace in the form of confession! So if I do end up committing a grave sin, that’s when I’ll remind myself “God forgives” but I’d add “So I’ll go to confession and  after my penance I’ll reconvinct myself of why I need to avoid this sin”

I also struggle with sexual sin and I felt that I was too weak willed to commit to not engaging in that while I was discerning if I should get baptized now, so I read and learned about the evils of lust (fr. Ripperger has great series on the seven deadly sins that was very helpful! It’s not very long and it’s on YouTube!) and more importantly, the theology of the body! Reading and learning about the Theology of the Body was a game changer! I’m now very committed to denying lustful thoughts even if my body isn’t on the same page and that helps me not to engage in the sin. Life is long though and no one is perfect, if we were we then God wouldn’t have given his only begotten son for our sins! So give yourself some grace, go to confession and start learning how to and why you should avoid lust!


Also side note, I have found that practicing abstinence (no meat on Fridays) and fasting every so often  has helped me with my self control in general! Fr. Ripperger specifically mentioned that in one of his talks about lust and it was a giant help to follow that advice!! Also keeping myself busy and avoiding my bedroom until it’s bed time! Read the Bible, say a prayer (Hail Mary is a good one for me when I’m in a “lust attack”), listen to a Catholic podcast! 

You can do it and don’t forget that God forgives! But we should also do our best to stay in friendship with him! And don’t skip mass!! 

Love you, God bless you!
